_about: THE SHRINKING OFFENDER LIST for `make docs-audit`'s `ste offenders` row (D226; D280, which retires D229's pinned per-file ratio). files: file -> lane (who owes the fix) and rule -> entries. An entry is `<hash> <label>`: the hash is the offending sentence's identity (scripts/ste_measure.py:offender_identity), the label is its first words for the person who rewrites it, and only the hash is compared. A sentence written twice is listed twice. A decision entry is keyed by its file tail (`docs/decisions/*-<slug>.md`), so a claim that numbers it moves nothing. The row FAILS on an offending sentence this list does not name, on an entry that matches nothing (stale: delete it), and on an entry the list at the merge-base with origin/main did not hold (growth), unless its rule is not in `rules` at the merge-base. A new file starts clean. A lane that rewrites a sentence deletes its entry in the same commit. `make offenders-prune` does that delete and never adds an entry. Never add an entry to excuse new prose. `rules` must equal the linter's ERROR-severity codes.
